items.question: ENGINE FIRE IN FLIGHT — What is the first action?
items.explanation: Stabilize the helicopter in safe OEI condition before further actions.

items.question: ENGINE FIRE ON GROUND — Which initial action sequence is correct?
options: Shutdown affected engine; discharge extinguisher; stop rotor
Start APU; brief passengers; land later
Raise collective; increase speed; set ECS OFF
Discharge extinguisher; keep engine running; hold 100% NR
items.explanation: On ground: stop the engine, discharge extinguisher, then stop rotor.

items.question: ENG DRIVE SHAFT FAILURE — Typical initial indication?
options: Rapid drop of affected engine TQ to ~0 with NF above NR
Gradual increase in TQ with NF droop
items.explanation: A drive shaft failure unloads the engine showing ~0% TQ while NF overspeeds above NR.

items.question: ENG OIL PRESS LOW — Recommended action?
options: Affected engine — Shutdown in emergency; establish safe OEI; land as soon as practicable
Increase power on affected engine to restore pressure
Pull FIRE T‑handle on unaffected engine
items.explanation: Low oil pressure may quickly lead to failure — secure the engine and fly OEI.

items.question: MGB OIL PRESS LOW — What is the landing recommendation?
items.explanation: Main gearbox lubrication loss is critical — immediate landing is required.

items.question: MGB OIL TEMP HIGH with normal pressure — Action?
options: Reduce power/airspeed as required; monitor; land as soon as practicable
items.explanation: Reduce loads and monitor. If persists or worsens, land promptly.

items.question: ROTOR LOW NR — Immediate action?
items.explanation: Lowering collective unloads the rotor and restores NR.

items.question: ROTOR HIGH NR — Immediate action?
options: Raise collective to reduce NR within limits
items.explanation: Raising collective increases rotor load and reduces NR back within limits.

items.question: DOUBLE DC GENERATOR FAILURE — Correct immediate action?
options: Shed non‑essential loads; land when practicable
Select APU — START and continue flight
Cycle GEN switches repeatedly until both online
items.explanation: Shed load to essentials and plan a precautionary landing.

items.question: ENGINE FAILURE IN FLIGHT (ENG OUT) — Initial crew actions?
options: Establish safe OEI; hold NR; identify engine
Lower collective to idle power and descend to 40 KIAS
Pull FIRE T‑handle on both engines
APU — START; ECS — OFF; continue normal flight
items.explanation: Stabilize, maintain NR, identify/confirm the failed engine and proceed OEI.

items.question: SINGLE ENGINE LANDING — What is generally recommended?
options: Plan OEI approach; land when practicable
Maintain 100% power on operative engine until touchdown
items.explanation: A controlled OEI landing mitigates risk of secondary failures.

items.question: DUAL ENGINE FAILURE — Immediate action?
options: Enter autorotation; adjust collective to maintain NR
Attempt immediate restart on both engines before rotor actions
items.explanation: Preserving NR is paramount — enter autorotation and manage energy.

items.question: ENGINE RELIGHT IN FLIGHT — When should it be attempted?
options: Only if time/altitude permit and relight conditions are met; otherwise land promptly
Always immediately after flameout regardless of conditions
Only after both engines have failed
items.explanation: Follow in‑flight relight conditions/procedure; prioritize aircraft control.

items.question: ENGINE CHIP — Recommended action?
options: Monitor parameters; consider shutting down affected engine if abnormal; land as soon as practicable
Continue flight to destination with no change
items.explanation: Chip detection warrants close monitoring and precautionary landing.

items.question: MGB CHIP — Recommended action?
options: Monitor indications; avoid high power; land as soon as practicable
Immediate shutdown of both engines in flight
Climb to reduce load then continue
items.explanation: A chip in the main gearbox requires caution and a prompt landing.

items.question: TRGB OIL PRESS LOW — Landing recommendation?
options: Climb to reduce tail rotor load
items.explanation: Tail rotor gearbox pressure loss can rapidly degrade yaw control.

items.question: TRGB CHIP — What is advised?
options: Monitor; avoid high yaw demand; land as soon as practicable
Immediate descent and continue to destination
items.explanation: Chip in TRGB: reduce loads and land to inspect.

items.question: HYD SYS 1 FAIL — General action?
options: Maintain control; AFCS as required; land as soon as practicable
Pull both HYD pumps CBs immediately
items.explanation: Single hydraulic system failure: control is retained but land prudently.

items.question: HYD SYS 2 FAIL — General action?
options: Maintain control; AFCS as required; land as soon as practicable
Immediate landing is mandatory in all cases
Turn off both systems to balance
items.explanation: As for single system fail: maintain control and land.

items.question: DUAL HYDRAULIC FAILURE — What is correct?
options: Reduce speed; avoid abrupt control inputs; land immediately
Maintain cruise speed; continue to destination
items.explanation: Without hydraulics, control forces rise significantly; land without delay.

items.question: AFCS/SAS FAILURE — Immediate consideration?
options: Hand fly; trim as required; land as soon as practicable
Turn AFCS back on repeatedly until it resets
items.explanation: Revert to manual control and land.

items.question: FADEC/EEC ABNORMAL (single engine) — Best action?
options: Match torque; avoid exceedance; land as soon as practicable
Shut down both engines in flight
Continue high‑power operation to test limits
items.explanation: Maintain safe power on both sides without exceedance and land.

items.question: XMSN OIL PRESS LOW CAS — What is required?
items.explanation: Transmission oil pressure low demands immediate landing.

items.question: XMSN OIL TEMP HIGH with normal pressure — Action?
options: Reduce power/airspeed; monitor; land as soon as practicable
items.explanation: Reduce loads, monitor, land if persists or associated with other warnings.

items.question: FUEL LOW — Recommended action?
options: Plan landing as soon as practicable
Descend and increase speed to burn evenly
items.explanation: Low fuel caution calls for a precautionary landing.

items.question: SUSPECTED FUEL LEAK — Best course?
options: Isolate suspected side if indicated; minimize risk; land as soon as possible
Maintain high power to accelerate consumption
items.explanation: Leak management is time‑critical; isolate and land.

items.question: FUEL FILTER BYPASS — What is advised?
options: Monitor; avoid contamination sources; land as soon as practicable
items.explanation: Bypass suggests contamination; plan a landing.

items.question: ELECTRICAL FIRE/SMOKE IN FLIGHT — First actions?
options: Non‑essential OFF; isolate source; land ASAP
Open doors and increase speed above Vne
GEN 1+2 — OFF then continue normal flight
items.explanation: Isolate, shed load, and land to address the fire source.

items.question: SMOKE/FUMES IN CABIN — What should be done?
options: Execute Smoke and Fumes Elimination; land as soon as possible
Descend below 500 ft AGL and continue
Shut down both engines in flight
items.explanation: Evacuate smoke/fumes and land promptly.

items.question: CABIN FIRE — Immediate action?
options: Use extinguisher as appropriate; land as soon as possible
items.explanation: Extinguish and land; underlying cause must be addressed on ground.

items.question: SEVERE MAIN ROTOR VIBRATION — What is correct?
options: Reduce speed; land as soon as possible
Increase speed to pass through resonance
items.explanation: Reducing speed lowers loads; land to investigate the source.

items.question: UNCOMMANDED YAW — Initial actions?
options: Check pedal response; reduce power as required; land as soon as practicable
items.explanation: Manage yaw with pedals and power; land for troubleshooting.

items.question: TAIL ROTOR DRIVE FAILURE — In hover/low speed, what is appropriate?
options: Shut down both engines at altitude
items.explanation: Loss of tail rotor thrust at low speed: land immediately by lowering collective.

items.question: TAIL ROTOR DRIVE FAILURE — In forward flight, recommended?
options: Enter autorotation if yaw cannot be controlled; perform power‑off landing
Continue with high power to maintain heading
Climb to high altitude and troubleshoot
items.explanation: If yaw is uncontrollable, reduce torque by entering autorotation and land.

items.question: AUTOROTATION — To correct low NR, the pilot should:
items.explanation: Priority is preserving rotor RPM by unloading the rotor.

items.question: AUTOROTATION — Flare and landing sequence:
options: Flare to reduce rate/speed; level; raise collective to cushion
Raise collective early at high speed
Keep nose down throughout; touchdown fast
Reduce speed first, then steep climb
items.explanation: Standard energy management for autorotative landing.

items.question: ENGINE OVERTORQUE — What is correct?
options: Reduce collective to within limits; land as soon as practicable; record exceedance
items.explanation: Avoid further exceedance and land for maintenance action.

items.question: ENGINE OVERTEMP/OVERLIMIT — Recommended?
options: Reduce power; monitor; land as soon as practicable
items.explanation: Power reduction and precautionary landing mitigate damage risk.

items.question: ICING SEVERE (encountered) — General action?
options: Exit icing conditions; use anti‑ice as available; land as soon as practicable
Climb into colder air to continue
items.explanation: Leave severe icing promptly; systems may not ensure safety in severe icing.

items.question: SMOKE SOURCE UNKNOWN — Which is correct?
options: Non‑essential OFF; isolate buses; ventilate; land ASAP
Increase cabin heat to burn off moisture
items.explanation: Treat as potential electrical fire until identified; land.

items.question: GENERATOR OVERLOAD — Crew action?
options: Shed non‑essential loads; monitor; land as soon as practicable
Turn off all equipment immediately and continue flight
Ignore unless a warning comes on
items.explanation: Protect electrical system margin and plan landing.

items.question: BATTERY OVERHEAT/SMOKE — What should be done?
options: Isolate battery per checklist; land as soon as practicable
items.explanation: Thermal events require isolation and landing.

items.question: DOOR OPEN/UNLATCHED IN FLIGHT — Appropriate response?
options: Reduce speed; avoid abrupt maneuvers; land when practicable
items.explanation: Aerodynamic effects increase with speed; land to secure door.

items.question: PRESSURIZED SYSTEM LEAK (hydraulic) — Indications and action?
options: Fluid smell/visible leak; monitor quantities; land as soon as practicable
Increase system pressure by power increase
items.explanation: Loss indications warrant a precautionary landing.

items.question: LANDING WITH TAILWIND REQUIRED (abnormal) — Safer choice during emergency?
options: Prefer landing into wind; if not possible, minimize tailwind and rate of descent
Climb and wait for wind shift
items.explanation: Wind management reduces loads and yaw risk during emergency landing.

items.question: ENGINE FAILURE DURING HOVER — Immediate action?
options: Lower collective to cushion touchdown; maintain attitude
Accelerate to 45 kt before lowering collective
items.explanation: Lower collective to preserve NR and cushion landing.

items.question: ENGINE INDICATIONS MISMATCH (torque split) — Best response?
options: Adjust collective smoothly to avoid exceedances; monitor; land as soon as practicable
Increase power to the lower‑reading engine
items.explanation: Maintain safe power sharing and plan a landing for troubleshooting.

items.question: ECS SMOKE/ODOR — What is correct?
options: ECS — OFF; ventilate; land as soon as practicable
items.explanation: Switch off the suspected source and land.

items.question: INADVERTENT IMC DURING EMERGENCY — Priority?
options: Attitude, Heading, Power; stabilize first, then navigate and communicate
items.explanation: Aviate‑Navigate‑Communicate discipline is critical.

items.question: POST‑FIRE/SMOKE LANDING — After landing, what is correct?
options: Emergency shutdown; evacuate; do not approach until safe
items.explanation: Secure and evacuate; treat as hazardous until inspected.
